item.title: Stationary Measures and Boundary Correlations for Multispecies Half-Line ASEP
item.description: arXiv:2610.34530v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct stationary measures of the multispecies ASEP on the positive half-line, with injection of highest-priority particles at the left boundary, using vertex models. Our results extend existing constructions of Martin and Aggarwal-Nicoletti-Petrov for the full-line ASEP to the half-line. For the two-species process, we compute the joint distribution of occupation colors at the first two sites. We also partially address the connection with the half-space ASEP speed process.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Bufetov, Yuan Tian

item.title: Scattering for the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map and the Steklov spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2610.34588v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop scattering theory for Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DtN) maps on asymptotically conic, unbounded domains $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^d$, that are only Lipschitz inside a compact set and whose boundary extends to infinity. Specifically, we prove a limiting absorption principle and demonstrate existence of the scattering matrix. As an application of the theory, we show that the eigenvalues of Steklov-type problems on curvilinear polygons, $\mathcal{P}$, are well approximated by the eigenvalues of a Dirac operator on $\partial\mathcal{P}$ whose transmission coefficients between edges meeting at a corner are given by the scattering matrix for DtN maps on asymptotically conic domains associated to the corners. Up to an arbitrary loss in the power of the eigenvalue, the error in the approximation is optimal among all possible asymptotics that use only local information about $\partial\mathcal{P}$.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Galkowski, Marcello Malagutti, Ruoyu P. T. Wang

item.title: The Inhomogeneous Kinetic FPUT Equation near Rayleigh-Jeans Equilibria
item.description: arXiv:2610.34636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the nonlinear dynamics of the spatially inhomogeneous kinetic wave equation associated with the FPUT-$\beta$ problem. We prove global-in-time well-posedness near nonsingular Rayleigh-Jeans equilibria and their asymptotic stability in particular in weighted $L^\infty$ norms in space and momentum, for small initial perturbations orthogonal to the collision kernel at almost every spatial point. We describe the spectrum near the origin at small spatial frequencies, identifying two simple eigenvalues with fractional and diffusive orders $|\xi|^{8/5}$ and $\xi^2$, respectively. Combining this spectral analysis with energy estimates taking into account the transport effect, we establish algebraic decay for the linear semigroup despite the absence of a spectral gap for the collision operator. We then use these estimates to obtain nonlinear stability.
item.dc:creator: Angeliki Menegaki, Haoling Xiang

item.title: Uniform Large Deviations, Barrier Identity and the N\'eel--Arrhenius Law for the One-Dimensional Stochastic Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.34823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the one-dimensional stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation with a regularised, multiplicative, degenerate trace-class noise of strength sqrt(eps), the regularisation being Q_delta^{1/2} = (I + delta A^{beta/2})^{-1}, A = -d^2/dx^2, beta > 3/2, and determine the exponential rate of thermally induced magnetisation reversal. (i) Uniform large deviations at fixed delta: for every delta > 0 the solution satisfies a large deviation principle on C([0,T];H), with a good rate function, uniformly in the initial datum over a V-bounded set with compact H-closure; no non-degeneracy of the noise is assumed. (ii) Removal of the regularisation: as delta tends to 0 the noise tends to space-time white noise. With U_delta the state-space quasi-potential and U_0 that of the limiting control problem (Q_0^{1/2} = I), U_delta converges to U_0 in the Gamma-sense, and the barrier is delta-independent: the infimum of U_delta over the boundary of D equals that of U_0 and equals c_* times the infimum of the micromagnetic energy E over that boundary, c_* = 2 lambda_2/(lambda_1^2 + lambda_2^2), under two structural assumptions only and with no geometric or transversality input. Pointwise convergence fails, so the Gamma-limit is the sharp form of the statement. (iii) Neel-Arrhenius law: combining (i) and (ii) with the classical exit-time theorem, the escape time tau from D = {E < r} satisfies both levels of the law - for every fixed delta > 0, eps log E[tau] converges, uniformly on compact subsets of the initial set, to the barrier, and lim_{delta->0} lim_{eps->0} eps log E[tau] = c_* times the infimum of E over the boundary of D. The Arrhenius exponent is therefore stable under the regularisation of the noise and is determined by the micromagnetic energy alone.
item.dc:creator: Zdzis{\l}aw Brze\'zniak, Fan Gu, Liang Li

item.title: Classification of Finite-Dimensional Simple Novikov Algebras and Their Irreducible Bimodules in Positive Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.34896v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a complete classification of finite-dimensional simple Novikov algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>2$, including families missing from earlier classifications in \cite{Osborn1992, Xu1996}. We determine explicit normal forms and all isomorphisms between them, and classify all nontrivial irreducible bimodules over these algebras.
item.dc:creator: Dong Liu, Yufeng Pei, Limeng Xia

item.title: Faithful Localization of Vertex Algebra Modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.34953v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a Faithfulness Theorem for vertex algebra modules, showing that two complementary geometric localizations can jointly detect global algebraic structure. We apply this principle to vertex algebras obtained by BRST reduction from classical invariant theory and identify them, under natural geometric hypotheses, with global sections of sheaves of chiral differential operators. As consequences, we prove vanishing of BRST cohomology in nonzero degrees and simplicity, and show that every finitely strongly generated module is a finite direct sum of copies of the vacuum module. In particular, the corresponding module category is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces. For families associated with classical groups, we identify the associated varieties with Hamiltonian reductions, proving quasi-lisse-ness and the predicted identification with Higgs branches of the corresponding supersymmetric gauge theories. This provides geometric realizations of a broad class of vertex algebras arising from three- and four-dimensional quantum field theories.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Arakawa, Xuanzhong Dai, Bailin Song

item.title: Membership in the cone of quantum states over time is NP-hard
item.description: arXiv:2610.34972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A state over time (stote) pairs a state $\rho$ with a channel $\mathcal{E}$ as the Hermitian, generally non-positive operator $(\rho\otimes\mathbf{1})\star J_\mathcal{E}$. Characterizing the convex cone $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ these operators generate was posed as an open problem in~\cite{HoogstederCalsamigliaWinter2025}. We exhibit a linear copy of the bipartite separable cone as an exposed face of $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$: for output systems of the form $B = A'R$ with $A'$ a copy of the input, there is an explicit witness $W_0\in\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}^*$ and an explicit injective linear map $L$ with $\sigma\in \mathrm{SEP}_{+}(A{:}R)\iff L(\sigma)\in\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}(A{:}A'R)$. Composing with the NP-hardness of separability shows that exact membership, weak membership, and weak optimization are NP-hard for $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}$ and its dual. A quantitative stability bound makes the weak-membership reduction valid at inverse-polynomial accuracy. Thus polynomial-time membership tests do not exist unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. Independently of this complexity assumption, Fawzi's theorem implies that $\widehat{\mathcal{Q}}(A{:}A'R)$ admits no finite semidefinite representation when $d=\dim A\ge2$, $r=\dim R\ge2$, and $d+r>5$.
item.dc:creator: Matt Hoogsteder-Riera

item.title: Trajectory Functionals in the Thermodynamics of Radiation-Induced Damage in Structural Materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.34983v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper delivers a novel self-consistent non-local kinetic framework based on dose-dependent semi-Markov renewal transport and the generalized Doob's h-transform to evaluate the structural degradation of WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings. By leveraging the Feynman-Kac formalism, we map the continuous microscopic defect path trajectories generated by the Liouville operator directly onto the evolution of the macroscopically integrated damage potential. The framework accounts for long-range memory effects in the degradation kinetics via a non-vanishing structural commutator of the path Liouville operator and Zwanzig-Mori projection operators, which mathematically links the spatial restrictions of microscopic sinks to energetic path penalties. Spatial profiling of the cladding's mean lifetime, demonstrates a distinct sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory encompassing distinct incubation, linear growth, and avalanche breakdown stages. The numerical results reveal an abrupt, localized reduction in the operational lifespan near the cladding boundaries. This marginal vulnerability is shown to be a direct physical consequence of boundary stress field singularities at the fuel cladding interface and localized embrittlement. The developed path integral architecture provides a strict thermodynamic link between non-equilibrium fluctuations and the global Griffiths macro-barrier, offering a robust predictive tool for high-burnup nuclear fuel safety assessments.
item.dc:creator: V. V. Ryazanov

item.title: The $C^0$-inextendibility of Kerr spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the $C^0$-inextendibility of the full Kerr realizations considered in this paper and all their connected covering spacetimes. The result holds for positive mass and nonzero rotation in the subextremal, extremal, and overextremal regimes. The obstruction at the singular ring is expressed by unbounded proper time in a fixed-endpoint causal homotopy class. It persists under every positive continuous conformal rescaling and under continuous widening of the Kerr causal cones, without any global causality assumption. We give sharp bounds in a fixed coordinate norm for stationary and axisymmetric perturbations and describe complete timelike geodesics that encounter arbitrarily large curvature near the ring.
item.dc:creator: Bobby Eka Gunara

item.title: Instability of exact finite-amplitude acoustic-gravity waves
item.description:
arXiv:2610.35210v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Godin (	extit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 767, 2015, pp. 52--64) showed that compressible fluids in a uniform gravity field support finite-amplitude incompressible wave motions, in which every parcel conserves pressure and density, and constructed exact Gerstner-type surface and edge waves, possibly carried by currents. Using the short-wavelength instability method for compressible flows, we show that these waves are linearly unstable above a critical steepness. The stability of each fluid level reduces to a Floquet problem depending on two parameters: the steepness $\mathfrak{e}=e^{ka_2}$ and $
u^2=(1-\mathfrak{e}^2)
u_0^2$, where $
u_0^2=\cos^2\alpha\,N_0^2/\Omega^2$, $N_0$ is the buoyancy frequency of the hydrostatic reference state, $\alpha$ the inclination of the plane of motion and $\Omega=(gk\cos\alpha)^{1/2}$ the intrinsic orbital frequency. In an isentropic fluid, a level is unstable if $\mathfrak{e}>1/3$, recovering Leblanc's threshold for Gerstner waves (	extit{J. Fluid Mech.}, vol. 506, 2004, pp. 245--254) and extending it to compressible surface and edge waves; weak stable stratification lowers the threshold to $ rac13- rac{32}{81}
u_0^2+O(
u_0^4)$. In an isothermal atmosphere, $
u_0^2=\kappa\cos\alpha/(kH)$, where $H$ is the pressure scale height. For horizontal wavelengths near $5.5\,H/\cos\alpha$, principal subharmonic resonance makes the critical steepness vanish. For the fast airglow wave observed by Hecht et al. (	extit{J. Geophys. Res.}, vol. 107, 2002, D20, 4444), which Godin interpreted with his solution, the lidar temperature places the layer in which this interpretation is consistent on this resonance, where the critical steepness is typically 0.1 instead of $1/3$. Instability is confined to a layer beneath the free surface of surface waves and to a wedge at the shoreline of edge waves.
item.dc:creator: Christian Puntini

item.title: Log-Sobolev inequality for 2D $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ lattice gauge theory at all couplings
item.description: arXiv:2610.35286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the log-Sobolev inequality holds for the two-dimensional $SU(N)$ Wilson lattice Yang--Mills measure with arbitrary fixed inverse coupling $\beta$. The log-Sobolev constant depends on $\beta$ and $N$, but is uniform in the volume of the underlying lattice. The proof relies on a two-scale disintegration argument.
item.dc:creator: Jack Piazza, Hao Shen

item.title: Spectral zeta functions in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.35306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spectral zeta functions and zeta-regularized determinants encode the spectrum of an operator in analytic functions. Over the completion $\mathbb C_\infty$ of an algebraic closure of $\mathbb F_q((\pi))$, two features of characteristic $p$ break this classical picture. Complex powers have exponents that vary only continuously in $\mathbb Z_p$, not analytically. Scalar traces record eigenvalue multiplicities only modulo $p$. We develop a resolvent-based theory that treats these two obstructions separately. For the first, inverse Stieltjes duality turns suitable scalar resolvents into locally analytic spectral distributions on $\mathbb F_q[[\pi]]$. A single exponent of the Mellin transform already determines the distribution and the entire Mellin family. We characterize exactly which power series arise in this way, by a growth condition on Carlitz moments. The criterion depends on the support: bounded Taylor coefficients are not sufficient. For stationary digit measures, the transform is the unique fixed point of an explicit contraction. The first $q-1$ nonconstant moments recover the measure. For the second, we replace traces by the Frobenius defect $F/\sigma(F)$, where $\sigma$ raises coefficients to their $q$th powers. On power series with small coefficients, this map is a group automorphism that preserves Gauss distances, and a convergent infinite product inverts it. Polynomial defects produce entire functions. They characterize exactly the diagonal spectra that are finite unions of forward Frobenius orbits, counted with multiplicity. For the shifted Carlitz operator, the resulting Fredholm determinant is a normalized reciprocal of the Anderson--Thakur function, and its Newton polygon is determined exactly.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: From one particle to N particles: uniform transport-information and log-Sobolev inequalities for Coulomb gases on the torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.35350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study how a functional inequality satisfied by the one-particle conditional distributions of a Gibbs measure, with a constant independent of the positions of the other particles, can be propagated to the whole N -particle system, with a constant independent of N , when the interaction is singular. Our model is the Coulomb gas on the torus T 3 in the mean-field regime. We distinguish two mechanisms. The first one is a dependent tensorization, governed by Dobrushin-Wu interdependence coefficients. It yields uniform Poincar{\'e} and transport-information W 2 I inequalities with fully explicit constants. We explain why this mechanism does not extend to the log-Sobolev inequality: the Zegarlinski-type coefficients, which require pointwise bounds on the interaction, are infinite. The second mechanism is a tensorization with a defect. Using a uniform bound on the partition function due to Duerinckx and Jabin, it yields a uniform log-Sobolev inequality for the Coulomb gas on T 3 at small charge. We identify the assumptions on the interaction under which each mechanism applies. All the results are then extended to the two-dimensional Coulomb gas and to periodic Riesz gases 1/|x|^s , 0 < s $\le$ 1. The extension to d $\ge$ 4 is also discussed.
item.dc:creator: A Guillin (LMBP), W Liu (LMBP), B Nectoux (LMBP), L Wu (LMBP)

item.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a positive global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a positive local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. Our main tool is a reduction of $s$-principal compression to a rank-$k$ singular value perturbation. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.
item.dc:creator: Priyanka Grover, Hemant K. Mishra, Sarishti Singh, Temjensangba

item.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.35383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a relative BFK gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to L\"uck and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles.
item.dc:creator: Victor Kalvin

item.title: The role of density in phase transitions and new perspectives on theta functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35437v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $z\in \mathbb{H}:=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\Im(z)>0\}$ and $\Lambda:=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\Im(z)}}\big({\mathbb Z}\oplus z{\mathbb Z}\big)$, and set $ \theta(\alpha;z):=\theta(\alpha;\Lambda)=\sum_{(m,n)\in\mathbb{Z}^2}e^{-\pi\alpha \frac{|m+nz|^2}{\Im(z)}}. $ We study the minimization of the functional $\theta(\alpha;z)-b\theta(2\alpha;z)$ and establish a complete phase diagram for all $\alpha>0$ and $b\in(0,\sqrt{2})$. For $0<b<\sqrt{2}$, an explicit threshold $b_1=0.0767767081\cdots\in(0,1/10)$ separates two distinct types of phase transitions. Type I: $0<b<b_1$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--rhombic--square--rectangular'' phase transition. Type II: $b_1\le b<\sqrt{2}$: it admits a type of ``hexagonal--square--rectangular'' phase transition, without passing through the rhombic lattices. These phase transitions contrast with Montgomery's theorem \cite{Mon1988}, where the hexagonal lattice minimizes the single theta function at all scales, and the recent B\'{e}termin-Faulhuber-Steinerberger theorem \cite{BFS2026} for translated Gaussian lattice sums, where the hexagonal lattice prevails in a min-max structure. In our setting, the density parameter $\alpha$ governs the sequence of optimal lattice shapes, while the competition parameter $b$ controls the emergence of the rhombic phase, which exists for $b<b_1$ and vanishes for $b\ge b_1$. As an application, we resolve B\'etermin's conjecture \cite{Betermin2021AHP}. B\'etermin predicted a Type I phase transition for the functional $\theta(\alpha;z)-(1/10)\theta(2\alpha;z)$ with $b=1/10$. We instead rigorously establish that no rhombic lattice is a global minimizer at any density and prove that the system undergoes a Type II phase transition, thereby settling the conjecture in corrected form.
item.dc:creator: Kaixin Deng, Senping Luo

item.title: Pentagon Equation in Deformation Quantization of Character Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.35446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deformation quantizations of the moduli space of framed flat bundles live naturally in the Drinfeld category. Such quantizations were constructed using the so-called quantum fusion by Li-Bland and \v{S}evera. We give a complete characterization of the dependence of this quantization on combinatorial choices, and prove that these quantizations are all isomorphic, forming vertices of an explicitly constructed complete commuting graph of algebra isomorphism. To this end, we extend the Kontsevich integral methods of Le and Murakami from even associators to all associators. Finally, we also prove that bi-invariant Haar measures provide traces on these quantizations.
item.dc:creator: J\'an Pulmann

item.title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.35507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Onofrio, Kamel Ourabah, Carlo Presilla

item.title: Geometric aspects of fault tolerance
item.description: arXiv:2610.35513v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We highlight three geometric aspects of fault tolerance. First, we construct an operator-algebraic formulation of the fiber bundle framework for fault tolerance, and show that a generalization of the Knill-Laflamme conditions implies a flat connection for this framework. Next, we develop this framework for Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. We show that, for each polarization type, their moduli space embeds smoothly into a Grassmannian of finite-dimensional subspaces of a regularized distribution space. Finally, we explain how GKP codes associated with Jacobians give rise to magic states that can be obtained by code space projections of Gaussian states and identify a $\rm CCZ$-type magic state arising this way.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Conrad

item.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
item.description: arXiv:2610.35534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Elhamdadi, Bryce Virgin

item.title: Grothendieck rings of near-Tambara--Yamagami fusion categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.35574v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the Grothendieck rings of fusion categories over $\mathcal{C}$ containing a nonpointed Tambara--Yamagami fusion subcategory and exactly one further simple object. The subcategory necessarily has rank five, its invertible objects form the Klein four-group, and the coefficient $\kappa$ of the additional simple object in its tensor square belongs to $\{0,2,7\}$. Each of these three based rings is categorifiable. For $\kappa=0$, every category belongs, up to tensor equivalence, to the rank-one odd-component extension list of Choi--Lu--Sun. For $\kappa=2$ we construct an explicit unitary group-theoretical realization, and for $\kappa=7$ a realization is $\rm{Rep}(\rm{PSU}(3,2))$.
item.dc:creator: Jingcheng Dong, S\'ebastien Palcoux, Kai Wang

item.title: Competing coherence geometries in positive maps: positivity hierarchies, atomicity, and optimal entanglement witnesses
item.description: arXiv:2610.35758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a family of positive maps on qudits whose Choi operators combine two competing coherence patterns: independent exchange couplings and a collective set of diagonal couplings. For every mixed member of the family, we derive exact conditions for positivity, complete positivity, and all intermediate levels of k-positivity, and we determine the complete phase structure of decomposability and atomicity. The higher-positivity thresholds depend on the channel multiplicities, whereas the exact decomposability boundary is universal in scale-free coordinates. Its proof combines an explicit positive-plus-copositive decomposition with a matching family of positive-partial-transpose (PPT) states. The latter form PPT edge states whose detection region is an ellipse, or a disk after collective rescaling. An embedded-qutrit certificate shows that indecomposability and atomicity coincide throughout the mixed family. In contrast, the purely collective endpoint is decomposable over its entire positive interval. Finally, at maximal coherence, an explicit positive subtraction produces an atomic optimal entanglement witness with the spanning property and a strictly larger PPT- detection set. The study thus provides an exactly solvable setting in which k-positivity, decomposability, atomicity, PPT-edge-state geometry, and witness optimality can be compared in arbitrary local dimension.
item.dc:creator: Massimiliano F. Sacchi

item.title: Self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges with large end-to-end distance
item.description: arXiv:2610.35769v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-intersection local times serve as the Hamiltonian in the Gibbs measure of continuous polymer models, for which the end-to-end distance is a key quantity. We study multiple self-intersection local times of Volterra Gaussian bridges, \emph{i.e.}, Volterra Gaussian processes conditioned on their final location $a$, as $\|a\|\to\infty$. For $d$-dimensional $(2,\zeta)$-locally nondeterministic processes with $\zeta\in(0,2/d)$, we prove that these local times exist in every $L^p$. Under two further conditions on the kernel, the $p$-th moment of the $m$-multiple self-intersection local time of the bridge is of exact order $\|a\|^{-\gamma}$ for every integer $p\geqslant1$, with $\gamma=p(m-1)(2-\zeta d)/(2-\zeta)$. In the plane, for kernels $k(t-s)$ with $k(0)\neq0$ and under strong local nondeterminism, we restrict the double self-intersection local time to $\{t_2-t_1\geqslant\|a\|^{-\alpha}\}$, $\alpha>0$, and establish a phase transition: its expectation decays like $\exp(-c\|a\|^{2-\alpha})$, converges to an explicit positive limit, or grows logarithmically, for $\alpha<2$, $\alpha=2$ and $\alpha>2$ respectively.
item.dc:creator: Olga Izyumtseva, Wasiur R. KhudaBukhsh

item.title: The counts of parity-odd vs even late-growing permutations in the group $\mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ differ by $(-1)^p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35779v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A permutation $\sigma\in\mathbb{S}_n$ of objects $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is called \emph{late-growing} if its partial sums never exceed the respective partial sums of the `average' permutation (with the arithmetic mean $n^{-1}\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n i = (n+1)/2$ of $1,\ldots,n$ on average at each entry $\sigma(i)$): $\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma(i) \leqslant k\cdot (n+1)/2$ for all positive $k\leqslant n$. We prove that for $n=2p-1$ odd, the set $\Phi_p\subseteq \mathbb{S}_{2p-1}$ of late-growing permutations is partitioned into parity-even vs odd elements, $\Phi_p = \Phi_p^{+} \sqcup \Phi_p^{-}$, in an almost symmetric way: $| \Phi_p^{+} | - | \Phi_p^{-} | = (-1)^{p+1}$. The proof is constructive: by viewing the permutations $\sigma\in\Phi_p$ as constrained walks on the integral lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, we describe two filters that pair all but one element in $\Phi_p^{+}$ versus $\Phi_p^{-}$; the remaining walk $\sigma^*$ with monotonically growing step amplitudes determines the dominant parity subset.
item.dc:creator: Kian C. Shah, Arthemy V. Kiselev

item.title: The $\varepsilon$-smoothed Entanglement of Formation and its relation to the Moreau-Yosida approximation
item.description: arXiv:2610.35797v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe a family of convex continuous functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, on the set of states of a bipartite quantum system (consisting of finite-dimensional or infinite-dimensional subsystems) obtained by applying the Mora-Piani-Briegel construction of $\varepsilon$-measure (proposed in [Phys. Rev. A 109, 052413]) to the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) with the use of the trace norm distance in the role of basic metric. These functions are non-increasing in $\varepsilon$ and converge pointwise to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$. We conducted a detailed analysis of properties of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$, using (among others) the relationship between the family $\{E_{F,\varepsilon}\}_{\varepsilon\in[0,1]}$ and the family $\{E^\lambda_F(\rho)\}_{\lambda>0}$ of Moreau-Yosida approximations of the EoF explored in [arXiv:2609.30246]. We obtain a variational expression for the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ (which for $\varepsilon=0$ turns into the standard variational expression for the EoF). We also describe the weak subadditivity property of the functions $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ and analyse their continuity properties. The semicontinuity bounds for the EoF (presented in [Lob.J.Math., 46, 2632-2658],[arXiv:2404.07978]) allow us to obtain easily computable upper bounds on the rate of uniform convergence of the function $E_{F,\varepsilon}$ to the EoF as $\varepsilon\to0^+$ on the sets of states with bounded rank/energy of one of the marginal states. Applicability of the obtained results to other entanglement measures, in particular, to the relative entropy of entanglement, is discussed. As an auxiliary result, it is shown that for any state of an infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system, there exists a nearest separable state w.r.t. the trace norm distance. The non-uniqueness of such a state is also shown.
item.dc:creator: M. E. Shirokov

item.title: Operator limits of random matrices: Edge universality and sharp approximations
item.description: arXiv:2610.35808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish operator universality at the spectral edge of general Wigner matrices by showing that their suitably rescaled Lanczos tridiagonalizations, constructed from deterministic initial vectors, converge to the stochastic Airy operator with Dirichlet boundary condition. The result requires control of the entire tridiagonal structure on the scale relevant to the limiting differential operator. The Lanczos coefficients for non-Gaussian Wigner matrices are strongly dependent. We analyze their fluctuations by combining multi-resolvent local laws with quantitative control of Krylov subspaces and a comparison of the resulting Jacobi coefficients with those of the Gaussian ensembles. This approach identifies the limiting Brownian potential directly from the original matrix entries, without invoking Dyson Brownian motion in the step of Green function comparison. The resolvent limit yields joint convergence of edge eigenvalues, embedded eigenfunctions, and spectral measures. For Gaussian, Laguerre and circular $\beta$-ensembles we construct sharp couplings to the stochastic Airy, Bessel and Sine operators, preserving the finite-matrix laws. For fixed $\beta > 0$, their squared Hilbert-Schmidt inverse errors have almost-sure orders $n^{-1/3}, n^{-1}$ and $n^{-1}$, respectively, with $a > 0$ in the hard-edge upper bound. We also identify the positive leading order coefficient for the circular ensemble, whose second derivative jumps at $\beta = 2$.
item.dc:creator: Hyung-Gil Kwak

item.title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.35836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case. We first raise the angular momentum to the extremal value by rotating shear pulses of non-axisymmetric gravitational radiation, and then damp the incoming data exponentially along a long non-expanding neck. At the degenerate target horizon we invert the linearised problem at all angular frequencies, using a factorisation of a fourth-order angular operator into an angular Teukolsky-Starobinsky product. As an application, we construct one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data whose maximal development contains an exactly Schwarzschild apparent horizon and, at a later advanced time, an exactly extremal Kerr event horizon. This is the first rigorous counterexample to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum, and proves a second conjecture of Kehle and Unger.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Czimek

item.title: Convergence of Quantum Lindstedt Series and Semiclassical Renormalization
item.description: arXiv:2301.12728v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we consider the KAM renormalizability problem for small pseudodifferential perturbations of the semiclassical isochronous transport operator with Diophantine frequencies on the torus. Assuming that the symbol of the perturbation is real analytic and globally bounded, we prove convergence of the quantum Lindstedt series and describe completely the set of semiclassical measures and quantum limits of the renormalized system. Each of these measures is given by symplectic deformation of the Haar measure on an invariant torus for the unperturbed classical system.
item.dc:creator: Victor Arnaiz

item.title: BV Pushforward of Palatini-Cartan gravity
item.description: arXiv:2507.06279v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of this note is to show that the standard BV formulation of gravity in the Palatini-Cartan formalism is equivalent, using a BV pushforward, to an AKSZ-like version compatible with BFV data on the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Canepa, Alberto S. Cattaneo

item.title: Ground State Energy of Dilute Fermi Gases in 1D
item.description: arXiv:2509.00536v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the one-dimensional spin-$J$ Fermi gas, interacting through a general repulsive 2-body potential, and prove asymptotics of the ground state energy in the dilute limit. The asymptotic behaviour is given in terms of the ground state energy of a spin chain, which is the Heisenberg antiferromagnet in the case of spin-1/2 fermions. We determine similar asymptotics for the Lieb-Liniger-Heisenberg model, showing that a product trial state used by Girardeau is not optimal.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Agerskov, Robin Reuvers, Jan Philip Solovej

item.title: Teleportation=Translation: Continuous recovery of black hole information
item.description: arXiv:2512.11877v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The \textit{Teleportation=Translation} conjecture posits that the recovery of information from a black hole is dual to a geometric translation in the emergent spacetime. In this paper, we establish this equivalence for general local quantum field theories by constructing a continuous unitary interpolation that bridges discrete algebraic teleportation protocols and continuous modular flow. We resolve the failure of dynamic idempotency, fundamentally inherent in Type III von Neumann algebras, by employing the Haagerup-Kosaki crossed-product construction. This lift to the semifinite Type~II$_\infty$ envelope yields a canonical, dynamically consistent path. Crucially, we prove that its unique infinitesimal generator $\tilde{G}$ is exactly twice the geometric modular momentum ($\tilde{G}=2P$). We establish this identity as a closed operator equivalence using Nelson's analytic vector theorem and quantify its structural robustness via non-commutative $L^p$ theory. Ultimately, our results demonstrate that unitary information recovery fundamentally manifests as a continuous geometric translation. This provides a rigorous operator-algebraic mechanism for resolving the black hole information paradox, offering a kinematic framework naturally extendable to include gravitational back-reaction.
item.dc:creator: Jeongwon Ho

item.title: Magnetic Hardy inequalities with singular integral weights
item.description: arXiv:2602.15665v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we present Hardy type inequalities for magnetic Dirichlet forms with singular integral weights. We analyze the local and global optimality of the integral weight and discuss several examples in details. An application of our results to spectral estimates for magnetic Schr\"odinger operators is provided as well.
item.dc:creator: Hynek Kovarik, Pier Cristoforo Rossaro

item.title: On a stability of time-optimal version of the Boundary Control method
item.description: arXiv:2604.02957v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega$ be a Riemannian manifold with boundary. The time-optimal version of the BC-method determines the parameters in the $T$-neigh\-bor\-hood $\Omega^T$ of $\partial\Omega$ from the boundary observations (response operator) $R^{2T}$ on the time segment $[0,2T]$. It visualizes the invisible waves supported in $\Omega^T$, by reconstructing the operator $W^T$ that creates these waves. The visualization is based on the triangular factorization of the operator $C^T:=W^{T\,*}W^T$ in the form $C^T:=F^{T\,*}F^T$ with a factor $F^T=U^{T}W^T$, where $U^T$ is a unitary operator. The factorization $C^T\mapsto F^T$ has certain continuity properties, due to which the time-optimal reconstruction $R^{2T}\mapsto C^T\mapsto F^T\mapsto W^T$ turns out to be continuous (stable) in the sense of relevant operator topologies (convergences). As an example, determination of the potential $q$ in the wave equation $u_{tt}-\Delta u+qu=0$ from $R^{2T}$ is considered. We show that $R^{2T}_j\to R^{2T}$ implies $q_j\to q$ in $H^{-2}(\Omega^T)$. However, the question of quantitative estimates of stability (the rate of convergence) remains open.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail I. Belishev

item.title: How to Untwist Twisted Gauge Fields
item.description: arXiv:2606.28888v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides an isomorphism between the space of twisted gauge fields on a principal bundle $\mathcal{P}(M,H)$ and the space of standard gauge fields on a different principal bundle $\mathcal{Q}(M,G)$ associated to $\mathcal{P}$. This isomorphism extends to local fields on the base manifold, which enables the use of local twisted fields in standard gauge theories (e.g. Yang-Mills-like theories). This allows one to deal with two symmetry groups, coming from $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$, respectively. The construction makes use of a larger principal bundle $\mathcal{S}$ which has $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ as quotient bundles. $\mathcal{S}$ is a Hilsum-Skandalis bibundle between the action groupoids $H\ltimes\mathcal{P}$ and $G\ltimes\mathcal{Q}$. The gauge structure on $\mathcal{S}$ encodes both standard and twisted gauge structures on $\mathcal{P}$. In addition, the isomorphism classes of bundles $\mathcal{S}$ up to an isomorphism covering the identity map on $\mathcal{P}$ are in 1:1 correspondence with the equivalence classes of cocycles (up to a coboundary). This paper also provides a new interpretation of (full) dressing fields as dynamic (or active) sections of a principal bundle.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Serge Lazzarini, Thierry Masson, Louis Usala, How to untwist twisted gauge fields, Journal of Geometry and Physics, Volume 231, 2027, 106028, ISSN 0393-0440
item.dc:creator: Serge Lazzarini, Thierry Masson, Louis Usala

item.title: The Dirac equation in (split-)octonions: origins, variants, and modern context
item.description: arXiv:2607.09703v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Octonions and split-octonions have been used to express the Dirac equation in physics in several conceptually distinct ways. This review organizes them into four groups: the 2-factor, 3-factor, and projection representations, which use (split-)octonion basis elements natively to model a spacetime basis, and the conventional use of octonions to carry Dirac algebra acting on spinors. For each group we identify the originating construction, relate later variants to it, and point to modern applications and to recent methods for native split-octonionic analysis. Because the multiplication table of the (split-)octonions is not unique, forms that look different in print can coincide after a norm-preserving linear isometry and a multiplication-preserving change of basis; we make such relations explicit and tabulate the basis conventions used across select sources. The 2-factor representation is treated in most detail: we document its origin and show that a recently proposed split-octonionic Dirac equation coincides with it after such an isometry and change of basis, while crediting the independent contributions of that work.
item.dc:creator: J. K\"oplinger

item.title: Wehrl-type entropy problem for compact connected semisimple Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.18919v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a compact connected semisimple Lie group, and let $\pi:G\to U(V_\lambda)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation associated with the highest weight $\lambda$. We prove that coherent projectors are the unique minimizers of the Wehrl entropy over all density matrices on $V_\lambda$. Similar extremal properties hold for power functions in place of the entropy function. The proof uses a second variation at the extremizer by perturbation in directions associated with Killing fields, similar to the strategy of Frank and Lieb used in \cite{FrankLieb}. Then the problem reduces to the uncertainty principle characterizing coherent states. This solves the Wehrl-type entropy problem for arbitrary compact connected semisimple Lie groups.
item.dc:creator: Haonan Zhang

item.title: The para--Racah Hamiltonian as an exactly solvable discretization of the P\"oschl--Teller box
item.description: arXiv:2609.30624v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The para-Racah polynomials, taken at the persymmetric value of their isospectral deformation parameter, define through their recurrence relation a mirror-symmetric tridiagonal Hamiltonian $J$. Its spectrum is a quadratic bi-lattice, the union of the squares $(s+a)^2$ and $(s+c)^2$ of two interlaced arithmetic progressions of unit step, and it exhibits fractional revival when the grid parameters $a$ and $c$ satisfy a Diophantine condition. As the number of sites grows, $J$ contracts to the trigonometric P\"oschl--Teller Hamiltonian on a finite interval. We establish this twice, on the recurrence relation and on the polynomials themselves. Both grid parameters survive in the limit, the difference $c-a$ as a scalar centrifugal term at the interior point fixed by the mirror, and $a+c-1$ as the strength of two confining singular walls at the ends. These walls turn the spectrum into the quadratic pair $(s+a)^2$, $(s+c)^2$, with Jacobi eigenfunctions $P_s^{(a+c-1,\,\mp(c-a))}$, and the two sublattices converge to two families that differ only by the sign of the second Jacobi parameter. The mirror symmetry of $J$ becomes the reflection about the midpoint, which grades the two families and carries the fractional revival to the limit. Algebraically, the bispectral pair of the discrete model, which generates the Racah algebra, becomes a pair of generators of the Jacobi algebra, one rung down the Askey--Wilson hierarchy, which is the dynamical algebra of the P\"oschl--Teller Hamiltonian.
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Z. Beaulac, Nicolas Cramp\'e, Quentin Labriet, Lucia Morey, Marlon Josue Rivera Valladares, Luc Vinet

item.title: $p$-adic spectral zeta functions via the inverse Stieltjes transform
item.description: arXiv:2609.33660v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spectral zeta functions provide a standard tool for regularizing determinants of differential operators in quantum physics. In a previous paper (J. Math. Phys. 66: 083505, 2025), we introduced a $p$-adic spectral zeta function for discrete spectra via a locally analytic interpolation function. In this paper we extend the framework to continuous spectra using the inverse Stieltjes transform. Starting from the resolvent of a bounded operator, we construct a generalized distribution, called the $p$-adic spectral distribution, and define bosonic and fermionic zeta functions and functional determinants. We establish their analytic properties, special value formulas, and Stirling expansions, and show that our previous framework is embedded into the present one in the discrete case. In this approach, the bosonic and fermionic cases exhibit an interesting symmetry. As an application, we consider the position operator in $p$-adic quantum mechanics on an arbitrary compact subset of $\mathbb{C}_{p}$.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: Strongly non-linear continuous model for wave propagation in 2D granular media: derivation and hyperbolicity analysis
item.description: arXiv:2610.31738v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we develop a nonlinear continuum model for wave propagation in two-dimensional granular materials, building on key ideas from Nesterenko's work. Starting from the Hertzian contact law and neglecting contact friction, we derive an effective continuum description through homogenization, assuming spherical, monodisperse grains, local periodicity, and the Cauchy--Born hypothesis. The resulting strain-gradient model depends on both the first and second gradients of the displacement field. We analyse the hyperbolicity of the leading-order system through its eigenvalues and eigenvectors, establishing conditions for hyperbolicity within a restricted deformation domain. The model is solved using an explicit finite-volume method to investigate gravitational settling and wave propagation. We derive analytical expressions for the longitudinal and transverse wave speeds and highlight their dependence on depth. Finally, the predictions of the continuum model are compared with existing discrete-element simulations. This formulation allows several extensions, including more complex packing geometries, contact laws, and large-deformation regimes in which the contact network can evolve.
item.dc:creator: Sebastiano Cominelli, R\'egis Cottereau, Sergey Gavrilyuk, Bruno Lombard, Fabien Petitpas

item.title: Synthetic geometry of differential equations: I. Jets and comonad structure
item.description: arXiv:1701.06238v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an abstract formulation of the formal theory partial differential equations (PDEs) in synthetic differential geometry, one that would seamlessly generalize the traditional theory to a range of enhanced contexts, such as super-geometry, higher (stacky) differential geometry, or even a combination of both. A motivation for such a level of generality is the eventual goal of solving the open problem of covariant geometric pre-quantization of locally variational field theories, which may include fermions and (higher) gauge fields. (abridged)
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Geometry and Physics v.231 (2027) p.106025
item.dc:creator: Igor Khavkine, Urs Schreiber

item.title: Velocity surface disorder of large deviation rates for high-dimensional random walk in strongly mixing environment
item.description: arXiv:2409.06581v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we establish the large deviation principles of random walk in strongly mixing environments. We show that the quenched and annealed rate functions share the same zero-set whose shape is either a singleton point or a line segment, with an illustrative example communicated and given by F. Rassoul-Agha. Furthermore, this paper reveals that under sufficiently low disorder, the two rate functions match on compact sets of both the interior and the boundary of the domain under finitely strongly mixing condition.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Chen

item.title: Asymptotic coefficients of Weil-Petersson volumes in the large genus
item.description: arXiv:2501.06421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mirzakhani-Zograf proved the large genus asymptotic expansions of Weil-Petersson volumes and showed that the asymptotic coefficients are polynomials in $\mathbb Q[\pi^{-2},\pi^2]$. They also conjectured that these are actually polynomials in $\mathbb Q[\pi^{-2}]$. In this paper, we prove Mirzakhani-Zograf's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Xuanyu Huang

item.title: Higher-order exceptional points in a non-reciprocal waveguide beam splitter
item.description: arXiv:2503.21445v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Non-Hermitian systems have attracted significant interest because of their intriguing properties, including exceptional points (EPs), where eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenstates coalesce. In particular, quantum systems with EPs exhibit an enhanced sensitivity to external perturbations, which increases with the order of the EP. Therefore, higher-order EPs hold significant potential for advanced sensing applications, but they are challenging to achieve due to stringent symmetry requirements. In this work, we study the dynamics of a generalized lossy waveguide beam splitter with asymmetric coupling by introducing non-reciprocity as a tunable parameter to achieve higher-order EPs even without dissipation. Moreover, we analyze the evolution of NOON-states under activated non-reciprocity, highlighting its impact on quantum systems. Our results open new pathways for realizing higher-order EPs in non-reciprocal open quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Shahram Dehdashti, Andreas Hanke, Ahmed Touhami, Janis N\"otzel

item.title: On the nature of the black hole information problem
item.description: arXiv:2505.17220v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The aim of this work is to present the black hole information problem and discuss the assumptions and hypotheses necessary for its formulation. As the problem arises in the framework of semiclassical gravity, we first review the necessary notions to describe Lorentzian manifolds equipped with physical properties, as well as the physical concepts of the theory that describes the gravitational interaction as the curvature of spacetime, general relativity. From its classical perspective, we develop the formalism to study the dynamical aspects of black holes in spacetimes obeying suitable causality conditions. Equipped with conjectures that nature censors naked singularities and that black holes reach a stationary configuration after they form, the black hole uniqueness theorems allow us to review several relations for the geometrical quantities associated with them. Following considerations of the other fundamental interactions, which are described by quantum field theory, we review the arguments in the formalism of quantum field theory in curved spacetime that give rise to the effective particle creation effect, its approximately thermal character, and the concept of black hole evaporation. With a precise quantification of information in quantum mechanics and assuming that the condition for physically acceptable states is given by the Hadamard condition, we review the result that entanglement between causally complementary regions is an intrinsic feature of quantum field theory. As a consequence, we discuss how the formation and complete evaporation of black holes leads to information loss. Conscious that such a prediction follows if no deviations from the semiclassical picture occur at the Planck scale, we discuss alternatives to this nonunitary dynamical evolution and formulate the black hole information problem. Lastly, we analyze the assumptions and hypotheses that lead to the problem.
item.dc:creator: Thiago T. Bergamaschi

item.title: Anyonic membranes and Pontryagin statistics
item.description: arXiv:2509.14314v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Anyons, unique to two spatial dimensions, underlie extraordinary phenomena such as the fractional quantum Hall effect, but their generalization to higher dimensions has remained elusive. The topology of Eilenberg-MacLane spaces constrains the loop statistics to be only bosonic or fermionic in any dimension. In this work, we introduce the novel anyonic statistics for membrane excitations in four dimensions. Analogous to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-particle exhibiting $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(2,N)}$ anyonic statistics in two dimensions, we show that the $\mathbb{Z}_N$-membrane possesses $\mathbb{Z}_{N\times \gcd(3,N)}$ anyonic statistics in four dimensions. Given unitary volume operators that create membrane excitations on the boundary, we propose an explicit 56-step unitary sequence that detects the membrane statistics. We further analyze the boundary theory of $(5{+}1)$D 1-form $\mathbb{Z}_N$ symmetry-protected topological phases and demonstrate that their domain walls realize all possible anyonic membrane statistics. We then show that the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ subgroup persists in all higher dimensions. In addition to the standard fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2$ membrane statistics arising from Stiefel-Whitney classes, membranes also exhibit $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics associated with Pontryagin classes. We explicitly verify that the 56-step process detects the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_3$ statistics in 5, 6, and 7 spatial dimensions. Moreover, in 7 and higher dimensions, the statistics of membrane excitations stabilize to $\mathbb{Z}_{2} \times \mathbb{Z}_{3}$, with the $\mathbb{Z}_3$ sector consistently captured by this process.
item.dc:creator: Yitao Feng, Hanyu Xue, Yuyang Li, Meng Cheng, Ryohei Kobayashi, Po-Shen Hsin, Yu-An Chen

item.title: Freidel-Maillet type equations on fused K-matrices over the positive part of $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$
item.description: arXiv:2512.00819v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The positive part $U_q^+$ of the quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_2)$ has a reflection equation presentation of Freidel-Maillet type (Baseilhac 2022). Its defining K-matrix has size $2 \times 2$ and can be expressed, using Rosso's embedding of $U_q^+$ into a $q$-shuffle algebra, as generating functions whose coefficients are Terwilliger's alternating PBW basis elements. This and older PBW bases of $U_q^+$ due to Damiani and Beck are unified by linear combinations of Catalan words (Ruan 2025). In this paper, we use this unification to define K-operators of any dimension $\geq 2$ in matrix form; the entries are explicit generating functions over $U_q^+$. Our main result is that any pair of such K-matrices, possibly of different dimensions, satisfy a Freidel-Maillet type equation. This yields a family of algebraic relations over $U_q^+$ that generalize Baseilhac's equation and can be used to study integrable systems or higher-spin representations. We conjecture that, for every spin, these K-matrices coincide with Lusztig's quasi R-matrix evaluated with its first leg on the corresponding finite-dimensional irreducible module.
item.dc:creator: Chenwei Ruan

item.title: An energy- and helicity-conserving enriched galerkin method for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2512.20109v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an enriched Galerkin (EG) method for the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations that conserves both kinetic energy and helicity in the inviscid limit without introducing any additional projection variables. The method employs an EG velocity space, which is the first-order continuous Galerkin space enriched with piecewise constants defined on mesh faces, together with piecewise-constant pressure. Two numerical schemes based on the rotational form of the convective term are proposed: a nonlinear scheme and a linear variant. Both schemes exactly preserve the discrete helicity and kinetic energy, and the Picard iteration maintains the conservation properties of the nonlinear scheme. We prove the conservation properties of both the methods, and establish stability and rigorous error estimates for the nonlinear scheme. Numerical examples demonstrate the accuracy and conservation of the proposed linear scheme.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Tong, Qilong Zhai, Qian Zhang, Ran Zhang

item.title: Geometric Complexity of Quantum Channels via Unitary Dilations
item.description: arXiv:2601.00735v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nielsen's geometric approach to quantum circuit complexity provides a Riemannian framework for quantifying the cost of implementing unitary closed-system dynamics. For open evolutions, the reduced dynamics is described by time-dependent families of quantum channels $\{\Lambda_t\}_{t\ge 0}$ admitting many inequivalent Stinespring realizations, so any meaningful complexity notion must specify which microscopic resources are counted and which transformations are treated as gauge. We develop a dilation-based geometric complexity framework that distinguishes implementation-dependent complexity, attached to a specific realization, from intrinsic channel complexity obtained by minimizing over a physically admissible class of dilations. The proposed functional is subtractive: it removes purely environmental contributions from the geometric cost of the joint unitary realization. The subtraction is derived from concise structural postulates --- closed-system consistency, environment-only neutrality, and invariance under dilation gauge transformations --- and admits a natural variational and geometric interpretation. We also define noise complexity as a companion quantity measuring the geometric deviation of a noisy implementation from a prescribed ideal closed-system evolution. In the Hilbert-Schmidt setting, we establish coherence-based lower bounds for unitary and noise complexity, prove linear time scaling under time-homogeneous dilation models, and obtain dissipator-controlled bounds in the Markovian GKSL regime. We illustrate the framework on canonical single-qubit benchmark channels: dephasing, amplitude damping, and Pauli/depolarizing noise.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Alberto Acevedo and Antonio Falc\'o 2026 J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 59 205303
item.dc:creator: Alberto Acevedo, Antonio Falc\'o

item.title: Explicit complex time integrators for stiff problems
item.description: arXiv:2601.07730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Most numerical methods for time integration use real-valued time steps. Complex time steps, however, can provide an additional degree of freedom, as we can select the magnitude of the time step in both the real and imaginary directions. We show that specific paths in the complex time plane lead to expanded stability regions, providing clear computational advantages for complex-valued systems. In particular, we highlight the Schr\"odinger equation, for which complex time integrators can be uniquely optimal. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these benefits extend to certain classes of real-valued stiff systems by coupling complex time steps with the Projective Integration method.
item.dc:creator: Jithin D. George, Julian Koellermeier, Samuel Y. Jung, Niall M. Mangan

item.title: Elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda and elliptic Toda chains: classical r-matrix structure and relation to XYZ chain
item.description: arXiv:2602.08143v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss the classical elliptic Toda chain introduced by Krichever and the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda chain introduced by Adler, Shabat and Suris. It is shown that these models can be obtained as particular cases of the elliptic Ruijsenaars chain. We explain how the classical $r$-matrix structures are derived for these chains. Also, as a by-product, we prove that the elliptic Ruijsenaars-Toda chain is gauge equivalent to discrete Landau-Lifshitz model of XYZ type. The elliptic Toda chain is also gauge equivalent to XYZ chain with special values of the Casimir functions at each site.
item.dc:creator: D. Murinov, A. Zotov

item.title: Integrable open elliptic Toda chain with boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2602.13903v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this letter we discuss the classical integrable elliptic Toda chain proposed by I. Krichever. Our goal is to construct an open elliptic Toda chain with boundary terms. This is achieved using the factorized form of the Lax matrix and gauge equivalence with the XYZ chain.
item.dc:creator: A. Zotov

item.title: Failing to keep the balance: explicit formulae and topological recursion for leaky Hurwitz numbers
item.description: arXiv:2603.06094v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently a new family of enumerative invariants called leaky Hurwitz numbers was introduced by Cavalieri-Markwig-Ranganathan in the context of logarithmic intersection theory. They admit an interpretation via tropical covers where the balancing condition fails. We employ tropical geometry to prove a generalisation of the piecewise polynomiality of Accadia-Karev-Lewanski for leaky completed cycles Hurwitz numbers, and a different wall crossing that is cubic instead of quadratic. Using tropical combinatorics and generatingfunctionology, we also find closed formulae for one-part and two-part completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers in genus $0$. Working more generally with a view towards topological recursion, we use Hamiltonian flows to associate spectral curves to very general cut-and-join operators. Under mild analytic constraints, we find the appropriate spectral curves, and in case the leakiness is fixed, we show that the resulting enumerative invariants satisfy topological recursion. This provides a partial inverse to recent work of Alexandrov-Bychkov-Dunin-Barkowski-Kazarian-Shadrin producing differentials satisfying topological recursion for KP $\tau$-functions. In particular these results specialise to completed cycles leaky Hurwitz numbers.
item.dc:creator: Marvin Anas Hahn, Reinier Kramer

item.title: On the existence of toric ALE and ALF gravitational instantons
item.description: arXiv:2604.15159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish existence and uniqueness results for asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) and asymptotically locally flat (ALF) gravitational instantons. In particular, we prove the existence of a unique, Ricci-flat, toric ALE and ALF gravitational instanton, for every admissible rod structure, that is smooth up to possible conical singularites. We also give an elementary proof that any toric ALE or ALF self-dual instanton is a multi-Eguchi-Hanson or multi-Taub-NUT solution.
item.dc:creator: Hari K. Kunduri, James Lucietti

item.title: Unveiling Topological Fusion in Quantum Hall Systems from Microscopic Principles
item.description: arXiv:2604.16525v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Establishing the fusion rules of anyonic quasiparticles in fractional quantum Hall fluids is essential for understanding their underlying topological order. Building on the conjecture that key topological properties are encoded in the ''DNA'' of candidate many-body wave functions - that is, the pattern of dominant orbital occupations restricted to a finite number of lowest Landau levels - we propose a combinatorial framework that derives these fusion rules directly from microscopic data. By extending Schrieffer's counting argument and introducing classes of topological excitations, our framework provides a unified route to the fusion rules for both Abelian and non-Abelian excitations. This approach elucidates the emergence of topological features from first principles in both fermionic and bosonic systems. In particular, we unveil the previously unknown fusion rules of the Hafnian fluid.
item.dc:creator: Arkadiusz Bochniak, Shinsei Ryu, J\"urgen Fuchs, Gerardo Ortiz

item.title: Perturbative Coulomb branches on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$: the global D-term potential
item.description: arXiv:2604.27066v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a Wilsonian description of perturbative D-terms in 4d $\mathcal N=1$ gauge theories on $\mathbb R^3\times S^1$ with chiral Kaluza--Klein spectra. A closed-form, one-loop-exact coefficient of the auxiliary D fields, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos parameters and globally valid throughout the holonomy space, determines the leading holonomy potential away from massless thresholds. We establish uniform weak-coupling control there and match across thresholds by retaining the light fields. Gauge-anomaly cancellation renders the Coulomb-slice vacuum equations affine within each chamber bounded by the thresholds, enabling exact linear analysis of their zero sets and numerical reconstruction through DBSCAN clustering of approximate zeros, LPCA denoising, and RANSAC hyperplane detection. Complementing the rank-one applications of the accompanying Letter, we study flavor-twist dependence in the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ $\mathcal N=4$ theory, and illustrate the numerical reconstruction in higher-rank R-twisted Argyres--Douglas reductions of interest in the SCFT/VOA correspondence. We also relate the same D-term data to leading stationary-phase equations of supersymmetric partition functions and a decompactification limit of the torus twisted superpotential.
item.dc:creator: Arash Arabi Ardehali, Daniel J. Resnick

item.title: Random Matrix Spectra from Boltzmann-Weighted Lattice Ensembles
item.description: arXiv:2605.21254v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a random matrix framework for studying statistical-mechanical lattice systems through spectral observables. Equilibrium configurations sampled from a Boltzmann measure are mapped to matrix ensembles whose covariance structure is inherited from the spatial correlations of the underlying model. This construction maps real-space correlation functions to a momentum-space variance profile, providing a direct bridge between statistical-mechanical correlations and correlated random matrix ensembles. We derive this variance profile in finite-correlation-length and critical regimes, and compute spectral moments within a Wick-contraction expansion. A complementary self-consistent description of the bulk density is developed using the resolvent formalism. These analytical methods are benchmarked against Monte Carlo data for the two-dimensional Ising model and three-dimensional Edwards--Anderson spin glasses. In both cases, the spectra evolve from the semicircle law at high temperature to model-dependent critical forms reflecting the structure of correlations. The framework, therefore, provides a quantitative spectral route to probing collective behavior in ordered and disordered statistical systems, while also defining a class of physically motivated correlated random matrix ensembles.
item.dc:creator: Yaprak \"Onder, Abbas Ali Saberi, Roderich Moessner

item.title: Integrable hierarchies with zero dispersion and elliptic curves
item.description: arXiv:2606.01354v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider integrable hierarchies such as KP, modified KP, 2D Toda lattice, BKP (small and large), DKP, Pfaff-Toda and their multi-component generalizations. We work in the framework of the bilinear formalism in which the universal dependent variable is a tau-function satisfying bilinear equations of the Hirota-Miwa type. Our principal interest in this paper is the dispersionless versions of the hierarchies. In the limit of zero dispersion the main object is an $F$-function, which is the limit of properly re-scaled logarithm of the tau-function. We show that in all the cases there exists an algebraic curve built into the structure of the hierarchy. We call it the {\it dynamical curve}. For the KP, modified KP and Toda lattice hierarchies, as well as for their multi-component generalizations, the curve is rational (of genus 0) and can be uniformized by rational or trigonometric functions. For hierarchies of the Pfaff type (DKP and Pfaff-Toda) the dynamical curve is in general a smooth elliptic curve (of genus 1), with its modular parameter being a dynamical variable. It is also shown that the large BKP hierarchy admits two different dispersionless versions. In one of them the dynamical curve degenerates to a rational curve while in the other one it remains to be elliptic. We show that a reformulation of the hierarchies based on uniformization of the dynamical curves by elliptic (or trigonometric) functions makes their structure nice and clear, especially in the multi-component case.
item.dc:creator: A. Savchenko, A. Zabrodin

item.title: Bayesian Variational System Identification with Weak-Form Residual Likelihoods
item.description: arXiv:2606.14942v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider system identification for discovering parameterized operators in governing partial differential equations (PDEs) from noisy spatiotemporal data. Building on variational system identification (VSI), which identifies PDEs through Galerkin weak-form residuals, we develop a Bayesian VSI (B-VSI) framework for operator selection, parameter estimation, and uncertainty quantification. The central idea is to define the likelihood directly in weak-form residual space by propagating observation uncertainty through the weak-form residual map. The resulting likelihood captures heteroscedastic and correlated residual errors while avoiding repeated forward PDE solves during inference. For efficient computation, we use lagged-covariance updates that yield generalized least-squares estimates and conjugate posterior approximations when applicable, together with gradient-based and particle-based methods for more general priors and posterior structures. Model-form uncertainty is handled through sequential operator elimination guided by a residual-space Bayesian information criterion. We demonstrate the framework on state-linear and nonlinear PDEs, including the Fokker--Planck equation and a two-field Cahn--Hilliard equation. The results show that B-VSI accurately recovers active operators and coefficients from noisy data, improves robustness relative to classical VSI, and provides posterior uncertainty estimates for coefficients and derived physical quantities.
item.dc:creator: Chengyang Huang, Siddhartha Srivastava, Krishna Garikipati, Xun Huan

item.title: $C$-networks and the planar Ising inverse problem
item.description: arXiv:2606.15082v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We solve the inverse problem for Ising models on reduced planar graphs in a disk, i.e., recovering the edge coupling constants from the boundary spin correlations. A recursive solution to this problem was provided by Galashin--Pylyavskyy. Our solution is nonrecursive. It is based on an Ising analog of the chamber ansatz which asserts that the inverse map factors through variables on the graph that transform under the Ising Y-$\Delta$ move according to the discrete CKP equation.
item.dc:creator: Yassine Elmaazouz, Terrence George

item.title: Involution-equivariant topological recursion and mirror symmetry for the affine binary dihedral Calabi--Yau threefold
item.description: arXiv:2607.07355v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a closed-string remodeling statement for the affine binary dihedral Calabi--Yau orbifold threefold $\mathcal X=[\mathbb C^2/\Gamma]\times\mathbb C$, where $\Gamma$ is a binary dihedral subgroup of $SU(2)$. This target lies outside the toric setting of the Bouchard--Klemm--Mari\~{n}o--Pasquetti remodeling conjecture: the toric mirror curve is replaced by the type-$D_l$ relativistic Toda curve of Brini--Ma--Strachan, and the Chekhov--Eynard--Orantin topological recursion is replaced by the $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant topological recursion of Giacchetto--Kramer--Lewa\'nski, run in the sign sector of the Toda-curve involution with the Prym kernel as its two-point input. We identify the equivariant orbifold quantum cohomology Frobenius manifold of $\mathcal X$ with the invariant Jacobian Frobenius structure of the Toda curve, and we prove that the B-model $R$-matrix, defined by regularized stationary phase, equals the A-side normalized canonical Givental--Teleman $R$-matrix on a chosen simply connected domain; this equality is anchored at the orbifold point through a semistable degeneration of the Toda curve. Comparing the resulting Givental--Teleman and Dunin-Barkowski--Orantin--Shadrin--Spitz graph sums then identifies, after a parity-twisted leaf substitution, the sign-sector recursion with the descendant Gromov--Witten generating functions of $\mathcal X$ in the stable range ($2g-2+n>0$ with $n>0$), and identifies the recursion free energies with the equivariant Gromov--Witten free energies of $\mathcal X$ for $g\geq2$. We also match the genus-one potential defined by the reduced calibrated tau function with the Gromov--Witten potential up to an additive constant.
item.dc:creator: Bohan Fang, Zhuoming Lan, Jingxiang Ma

item.title: Twisted Yangians of split types BI, CI, DI and Drinfeld type current relations
item.description: arXiv:2607.14692v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study twisted Yangians associated with the split symmetric pairs of types BI, CI and DI. We introduce a new presentation of these algebras, which we call the transposed presentation, governed by a twisted reflection equation that interacts naturally with the Gaussian decomposition of the generating matrix. Working entirely within the $R$-matrix presentation, we derive Drinfeld-type current presentations of the special twisted Yangian $SY^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ and of the extended twisted Yangian $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$, in which the Serre relations are stated in a closed current form. Extracting coefficients recovers the Drinfeld presentation of Lu, Wang and Zhang, in the normalisation of Lu. As a consequence, we establish an explicit isomorphism between the $R$-matrix and Drinfeld presentations conjectured by Lu, Wang and Zhang. As a byproduct, we obtain a tensor product decomposition of $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ into the twisted Yangian in the Drinfeld presentation and a polynomial ring in countably many central variables. We also obtain Poincar\'e-Birkhoff-Witt bases in the Drinfeld generators and the coideal coproduct on the low Drinfeld modes at all but the last node.
item.dc:creator: Vidas Regelskis

item.title: New bound on $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell locality of a nonseparable Werner state
item.description: arXiv:2607.18050v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In many quantum applications it is important to know whether or not a Bell nonlocal two-qudit state exhibits its nonlocality under correlation scenarios with some given numbers $S_{1},S_{2}\geq1$ of generalized quantum measurements at two sites. In the present article, we find analytically a new general condition sufficient for a nonseparable Werner state with a dimension $d\leq\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\}$ to satisfy all Bell inequalities under every $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting correlation scenario with outcomes of an arbitrary spectral type, discrete or continuous $-$ that is, to be $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell local, for short. For a variety of measurement settings $S_{1}, S_{2}$, this new general bound is beyond (i) Werner's and Barrett's locality bounds for a nonseparable Werner state and (ii) the related result by Johnson and Viola [Phys. Rev. A 88, 032323 (2013)] on "sharability" of this state. When specialized to $d = 2$ and $\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\} = 2, 3$, our new general bound improves upon the corresponding results by Terhal et. al. in [Phys. Rev. Lett. 90, 157903 (2003)], moreover, for $d=\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\} = 2$, it reduces exactly to the bound derived for this case via the CHSH inequality. We prove also explicitly in operator terms the result of Terhal et. el. that every nonseparable Werner state with a dimension $d >\min\{S_{1},S_{2}\}$ is $S_{1}\times S_{2}$-setting Bell local. The new results presented in this article are important for both the theory of Bell nonlocality and quantum applications based on this fundamental concept.
item.dc:creator: Elena R. Loubenets

item.title: Absence of hidden analytic conserved quantities in harmonically confined rods
item.description: arXiv:2607.18872v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Systems of hard rods of equal length in a one-dimensional harmonic trap have been observed to exhibit peculiar non-ergodic behavior that might suggest the existence of a novel hidden conserved quantity beyond the two well known ones, i.e., the total energy and the center-of-mass energy. In this work, we investigate this possibility by systematically constraining the forms of the conserved quantities, and we rigorously rule out the existence of any extra hidden conserved quantity that is analytic in the positions and momenta of the rods involved.
